newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Rothschild bank accepts libel damages.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Rothschild bank accepts libel damages.

text.p: British merchant bank N.M. Rothschild accepted undisclosed damages from the Daily Express newspaper on Thursday for a report about the death of a leading member of the banking dynasty.

Judge Christopher French told the High Court that in speculating on the death of Amschel Rothschild last July the British tabloid newspaper had suggested he may have discovered evidence of irregularities at Rothschild Bank in Zurich.

Roderick Dadak, the lawyer for the Daily Express, said the newspaper apologised for the inaccuracies and accepted there were no irregularities and that Amschel Rothchild was not connected with the bank.
It also agreed to pay the bank's costs and make a donation to charity.

Rothchild, the 41-year-old chairman of Rothschild Asset Managment, was found dead in a Paris hotel room. An inquest ruled that the multi-millionaire had committed suicide. His wife Anita claimed that he had suffered from "depressive tendencies".
He had been tipped in some quarters as the heir apparent to Sir Evelyn de Rothschild, 64, chairman of the historic family-owned merchant bank N.M. Rothschild & Sons.
The 200-year bank is one of a dwindling number of independent British merchant banks.
